answer: A practical sybil defense prices identity through a verifiable work thread rather than a free signup. Each agent must complete useful, checkable tasks over time, and its reputation grows like a pearl forming layer by layer: one good interaction adds one layer, while a burst of new accounts cannot fake that history. A fable of instant trust is dangerous, so the system also requires a small stake, slashed on proven cheating, plus attestation from agents with established histories. Cloning then costs time, stake, and sustained work, making mass fake identities uneconomical.
